input: head is None or the first node of a finite, acyclic singly linked list of n distinct node objects, with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Each caller-owned ListNode has ordinary writable data fields val and next; val is an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], and next is another node or None. No getters, proxies, custom assignment behavior or concurrent observers/mutations are allowed. External aliases may point at any input node and observe the final rewiring. k is a nonnegative integer in [0, 9007199254740991]. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The first original node after rotating the list right by k positions modulo its length. Empty input returns None. A singleton, k = 0 or any whole-length rotation returns the original head with unchanged links.
mutation_aliasing: Values and node identities are preserved. For a nonzero reduced rotation, the old tail next is set to the old head and the new tail next is set to None; all other next fields remain unchanged. A temporary cycle exists between these two assignments, which is why concurrent observers and assignment hooks are excluded. The final list is acyclic with exactly the original nodes. Caller aliases observe the final relinking. No node or sentinel is allocated, and the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Length, k, k modulo length and the nonnegative new-tail step count remain exact integers. Modulo is only evaluated for a nonempty list of at least two nodes, so its divisor is positive. Node values are not inspected or arithmetically changed.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space. One scan obtains length and old tail, and at most one further partial scan finds the new tail. Huge k is reduced by modulo, not repeated rotations. No recursion or node-array copy is used.
